```{r Libraries, include = FALSE}
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(tidyverse)
library(pheatmap)
library(grid)
library(forestplot)
library(parallel)
```


## Import Data
First, import the necessary data to run this pipeline. The clinical data, counts, and gene metadata were imported from TCGA using the **import_data.Rmd** script. The clinical data contains patient information about age, survival, etc., while the counts are the bulk RNA sequencing samples from their tumors. The gene metadata is used to match ENSEMBL IDs to common gene names.

Lineage markers were extracted from our lab's scRNA-seq clustering of publicly available cancer datasets. We extract top 20 differentially expressed markers from each cell type.

```{r Import Data}
cancer <- 'LIHC'

clinical_data <- read.csv(paste0(cancer, "_clinical.csv"), row.names = 1)
counts <- read.csv(paste0(cancer, "_counts.csv"), row.names = 1)
gene_metadata <- read.csv("BLCA_gene_metadata.csv", row.names = 1)
lineage_markers <- read.csv("Common_Lineage_Markers.csv") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), trimws))
```

## High Versus Low Expression of a Gene List
Stratify patients into high and low expression of `gene_list` by ranking by
each gene and taking the mean rank. Plot a heatmap of selected patient
expression of `gene_list`. Run a Kaplan-Meier survival analysis comparing patients
that are high versus low in expression of `gene_list`. Returns p value and how
big the difference was. If the difference is positive, the high group had better
survival. If the difference is negative, the low group had better survival.

```{r Define Single Lineage Function}
singleLineage <- function(gene_module, gene_list, clinical = clinical_data, makeHeatMap = FALSE, HR = FALSE) {
  
  # Code for TCGA Data
  # Ensuring consistent genes between datasets ----
  # Make sure all genes are in gene metadata
  valid_ensembl <- rownames(gene_metadata[gene_metadata$gene_name %in% gene_list,])

  # Make sure all genes are in bulk RNA seq
  valid_ensembl <- intersect(valid_ensembl, rownames(counts))
  desired_counts <- counts[valid_ensembl,]

  if (length(valid_ensembl) < 1) {
    return(c(1, 0))
  }

  desired_counts$gene_name <- gene_metadata[valid_ensembl, "gene_name"]
  rownames(desired_counts) <- NULL
  
  desired_counts <- desired_counts |>
    distinct(gene_name, .keep_all = T) |>
    column_to_rownames("gene_name")
  
  # Ranking patients by gene expression ----
  ranked_counts <- apply(desired_counts, 1, function(x) rank(-x, ties.method = "first"))
  
  # get the mean rank for each patient
  mean_rank <- rowMeans(ranked_counts)
  
  # get the upper and lower quartiles
  upper <- names(mean_rank)[mean_rank <= quantile(mean_rank, 0.25)]
  lower <- names(mean_rank)[mean_rank >= quantile(mean_rank, 0.75)]
  
  # Generating heatmap ----
  if (makeHeatMap) {
    heatmap_values <- cbind(ranked_counts, mean = mean_rank)
    heatmap_values <- t(heatmap_values[order(heatmap_values[,"mean"], decreasing = TRUE),
                                       -ncol(heatmap_values)])
    ngenes = nrow(heatmap_values)
    brewer_palette <- "RdBu"
    ramp <- colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(11, brewer_palette))
    mr <- ramp(256)[256:1]
    pheatmap::pheatmap(heatmap_values, labCol = NA, color = mr, scale = "row", 
                       fontsize_col = 10, fontsize_row = 200/ngenes, fontsize = 15, 
                       border_color = NA, show_colnames=FALSE, cluster_rows=FALSE,
                       cluster_cols=FALSE, main=gene_module)
  }
  
  # Kaplan-Meier ----
  # adding the significant counts data for patients (high and low) together 
  combined_patients <- data.frame(
    patients = c(upper, lower),
    stratum = rep(c("HIGH", "LOW"), c(length(upper), length(lower)))
  )
  
  # formatting patient labels to match clinical data
  combined_patients$patients <- gsub("\\.", "-", combined_patients$patients)
  
  # clinical data for high and low patients
  combined_patients <- merge(combined_patients, clinical, by.x = 'patients', by.y = 'cases')
  
  # adding a column for whether the patient is dead or not 
  combined_patients$deceased <- ifelse(combined_patients$vital_status == "Alive", FALSE, TRUE)
  
  # Overall survival (for TCGA data)
  combined_patients$overall_survival <- ifelse(combined_patients$deceased == TRUE,
                                               combined_patients$days_to_death,
                                               combined_patients$days_to_last_follow_up)
  
  final_plot_data <- as.data.frame(combined_patients)
  
  # Returning hazard ratio instead
  if (HR) {
    fit <- coxph(
      Surv(overall_survival, deceased) ~ stratum,
      data = final_plot_data
    )
    
    pval <- round(summary(fit)$coefficients["stratumLOW", "Pr(>|z|)"], 4)
    
    hr <- (exp(coef(fit))[1])
    
    ci <- exp(confint(fit)["stratumLOW", ])
    ci_lower <- round(ci[1], 3)
    ci_upper <- round(ci[2], 3)
    
    return(c(hr, ci_lower, ci_upper, pval))
  }
  
  # fitting survival curve
  fit <- survminer::surv_fit(Surv(overall_survival, deceased) ~ stratum, data = final_plot_data)
  
  # Outputs ----
  pval <- surv_pvalue(fit)$pval
  
  rmean_high <- summary(fit, rmean = "common")$table[, "rmean"][1]
  rmean_low <- summary(fit, rmean = "common")$table[, "rmean"][2]
  
  survival_dif <- (rmean_high - rmean_low)
  
  return(c(pval, survival_dif))
}
```

```{r Run Single Lineage Function}
singleLineage(gene_module = "NK Markers", gene_list = lineage_markers$Mature.NK,
              makeHeatMap = TRUE)
```


## High Versus Low Expression of All Cell Types
The `singleLineage()` evaluates whether patients high in a specific cell type
have better or worse survival than patients low in that cell type. This function
ranks cell types within a specific cancer by plotting the p value (magnitude)
and mean survival difference (direction).

```{r Define Lineage Heat Map Function}
LineageHeatMap <- function(lineage) {
  
  pvalues <- numeric(0)
  
  for (i in 1:ncol(lineage)) {
    
    # Subset the name of one cell type
    cell <- colnames(lineage)[i]
    
    # Draw lineage markers for that cell type
    markers <- lineage[,i]
    
    # Run singleLineage() on cell type
    result <- singleLineage(gene_module = cell, gene_list = markers,
                            makeHeatMap = FALSE)
    
    
    # Extracting p value (magnitude) and mean difference (direction)
    pval <- result[1]
    mean_dif <- result[2]
    
    # Identify if high cell population is good or bad
    if (mean_dif > 0) {
      pvalues <- c(pvalues, (-log10(pval)))
    } else {
      pvalues <- c(pvalues, (log10(pval)))
    }
  }
  
  # Creating the matrix for the heatmap that has each cell and its pval
  plot_data <- matrix(pvalues, ncol = 1, dimnames = list(colnames(lineage), "p-val"))
  
  # ordering the matrix
  plot_data <- plot_data[order(plot_data[,1], decreasing = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
  
  
  # plotting the heatmap 
  title <- paste("All cells in", cancer)
  
  brewer_palette <- "RdBu"
  ramp <- colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(5, brewer_palette))
  mr <- ramp(1000)[1000:1]
  rg <- 3
  
  plot <- pheatmap::pheatmap(plot_data, labCol = NA, color = mr, scale = "none",
                             fontsize_col = 10, fontsize_row = 10, fontsize = 15,
                             border_color = NA, show_rownames = TRUE,
                             show_colnames=FALSE, cluster_rows=FALSE,
                             cluster_cols=FALSE, main = title, display_numbers = TRUE,
                             number_format = "%.5f", number_color = "Black",
                             breaks = seq(-rg, rg, length.out = 1000))
  
  return(plot)
}
```


```{r Run Lineage Heat Map Function}
plot <- LineageHeatMap(lineage_markers)

ggsave(filename = paste0(cancer, '_single_lineage.pdf'), plot = plot, dpi = 300,
       units = 'in', width = 8, height = 12)
```

## High/High Versus Low/Low or High not High Expression of Two Gene Lists
First, we use `stratifyPatients()` to label HIGH and LOW patients in each cell
type. The `ratio` parameter is the percentile that we would like to deem as high
or low. The default is 0.25, which takes the top quartile as HIGH and the bottom
quartile as LOW.

The `HighHighLowLow()` command identifies synergistic interactions between two
cell types by comparing patients that are high in both cell types to patients
that are low in both cell types. Then we find patients that are HIGH in both
and compare them to patients that are LOW in both using a Kaplan-Meier survival
analysis (same as `runSingleLineage()`). The function returns the p value and
the mean difference in survival.

The `HighNotHigh()` command identifies the baseline effect of each cell type
in the absence of the other cell type. It subsets for when one cell type gene
list is high and the other cell type is not high. Then the same Kaplan-Meier
survival analysis is run, and the function returns the p value and mean
difference in survival.

```{r Define Stratify Patients Helper Function}
stratifyPatients <- function(gene_list) {
  
  valid_ensembl <- rownames(gene_metadata[gene_metadata$gene_name %in% gene_list,])

  # Make sure all genes are in bulk RNA seq
  valid_ensembl <- intersect(valid_ensembl, rownames(counts))
  desired_counts <- counts[valid_ensembl,]

  if (length(valid_ensembl) < 1) {
    return(c(1, 0))
  }

  desired_counts$gene_name <- gene_metadata[valid_ensembl, "gene_name"]
  rownames(desired_counts) <- NULL
  
  desired_counts <- desired_counts |>
    distinct(gene_name, .keep_all = T) |>
    column_to_rownames("gene_name")
  
  # Ranking patients by gene expression ----
  # order patients
  ranked_counts <- apply(desired_counts, 1, function(x) rank(-x, ties.method = "first"))
  
  # adding the mean rank across all rows 
  mean_rank <- rowMeans(ranked_counts)
  
  # upper and lower quartiles
  upper <- names(mean_rank[mean_rank <= quantile(mean_rank, 0.25)])
  lower <- names(mean_rank[mean_rank >= quantile(mean_rank, 0.75)])
  
  # Compiling clinical and counts data for the high and low patients ----
  # adding the significant counts data for patients (high and low) together
  combined_patients <- data.frame(
    patients = c(upper, lower),
    stratum = rep(c("HIGH", "LOW"), c(length(upper), length(lower)))
  )
  
  # formatting patient labels to match clinical data
  combined_patients$patients <- gsub("\\.", "-", combined_patients$patients)
  
  # adding clinical data to counts data
  combined_patients <- merge(combined_patients, clinical_data, by.x = 'patients', by.y = 'cases')
  
  # adding a column for whether the patient is dead or not 
  combined_patients$deceased <- ifelse(combined_patients$vital_status == "Alive", FALSE, TRUE)
  
  # Overall survival (for TCGA data)
  combined_patients$overall_survival <- ifelse(combined_patients$deceased == TRUE,
                                               combined_patients$days_to_death,
                                               combined_patients$days_to_last_follow_up)
  
  # exporting the final data to be used for plot 
  final_plot_data <- as.data.frame(combined_patients)
  
  return (final_plot_data)
}
```

#### High High Low Low
```{r Define High High Low Low Function}
HighHighLowLow <- function(gene_list1, gene_list2) {
  
  # Extract HIGH and LOW patients for both gene lists
  cell1_patients <- stratifyPatients(gene_list = gene_list1)
  
  cell1_upper <- cell1_patients[cell1_patients$stratum == "HIGH", ]
  cell1_lower <- cell1_patients[cell1_patients$stratum == "LOW", ]
  
  cell2_patients <- stratifyPatients(gene_list = gene_list2)
  
  cell2_upper <- cell2_patients[cell2_patients$stratum == "HIGH", ]
  cell2_lower <- cell2_patients[cell2_patients$stratum == "LOW", ]
  
  # Identify patients that are HIGH or LOW in both gene lists
  high_high <- cell1_upper[cell1_upper$patients %in% intersect(cell1_upper$patients, cell2_upper$patients), ]
  low_low <- cell1_lower[cell1_lower$patients %in% intersect(cell1_lower$patients, cell2_lower$patients), ]
  
  # Check for conditions: if either group has too little patients (<15) OR
  # there is a big difference in HIGH/HIGH vs LOW/LOW populations, return
  # no significance.
  if (nrow(high_high) < 15 || nrow(low_low) < 15) {
    return (c(1, 0))
  }
  
  if (abs(nrow(high_high) - nrow(low_low)) > 0.20*(nrow(high_high))) {
    return (c(1, 0))
  }

  # Collate all relevant patients for analysis
  final_plot_data <- as.data.frame(rbind(high_high, low_low))
  
  # Run Kaplan-Meier Survival Analysis ----
  fit <- survminer::surv_fit(Surv(overall_survival, deceased) ~ stratum, data = final_plot_data)
  
  pval <- surv_pvalue(fit)$pval
  
  rmean_high <- as.numeric(summary(fit, rmean = "common")$table[, "rmean"][1])
  rmean_low <- as.numeric(summary(fit, rmean = "common")$table[, "rmean"][2])
  
  mean_dif <- (rmean_high - rmean_low)

  return(c(pval, mean_dif))
}
```

#### High Not High
```{r Define High Not High Function}
HighNotHigh <- function(gene_list1, gene_list2) {
  
  # Extract HIGH and LOW patients for both gene lists
  cell1_patients <- stratifyPatients(gene_list = gene_list1)
  
  cell1_upper <- cell1_patients[cell1_patients$stratum == "HIGH", ]
  cell1_lower <- cell1_patients[cell1_patients$stratum == "LOW", ]
  
  cell2_patients <- stratifyPatients(gene_list = gene_list2)
  
  cell2_upper <- cell2_patients[cell2_patients$stratum == "HIGH", ]
  cell2_lower <- cell2_patients[cell2_patients$stratum == "LOW", ]
  
  # Identify patients that are HIGH or LOW in both gene lists
  high_nothigh <- cell1_upper[!(cell1_upper$patients %in% cell2_upper$patients), ]
  low_notlow <- cell1_lower[!(cell1_lower$patients %in% cell2_lower$patients), ]
  
  # Check for conditions: if either group has too little patients (<15) OR
  # there is a big difference in HIGH/HIGH vs LOW/LOW populations, return
  # no significance.
  if (nrow(high_nothigh) < 15 || nrow(low_notlow) < 15) {
    return (c(1, 0))
  }
  
  if (abs(nrow(high_nothigh) - nrow(low_notlow)) > 0.20*(nrow(high_nothigh))) {
    return (c(1, 0))
  }

  # Collate all relevant patients for analysis
  final_plot_data <- as.data.frame(rbind(high_nothigh, low_notlow))
  
  # Run Kaplan-Meier Survival Analysis ----
  fit <- survminer::surv_fit(Surv(overall_survival, deceased) ~ stratum, data = final_plot_data)
  
  pval <- surv_pvalue(fit)$pval
  
  rmean_high <- as.numeric(summary(fit, rmean = "common")$table[, "rmean"][1])
  rmean_low <- as.numeric(summary(fit, rmean = "common")$table[, "rmean"][2])
  
  mean_dif <- (rmean_high - rmean_low)

  return(c(pval, mean_dif))
}
```


## High/High Low/Low Versus High Not High Combinations of Two Cell Types
`TwoLineageHeatMapHHLL()` evaluates whether patients HIGH in both cell types
survive better than patients LOW in both cell types within a specific cancer.
This can be plotted on a heatmap of all interactions between all cell types
within the tumor.

```{r Define Two Lineage High High Low Low Matrix}
TwoLineageMatrixHHLL <- function(lineage) {
  
  # result matrix to store all the p-values 
  result_matrix <- matrix(nrow = ncol(lineage), ncol = ncol(lineage),
                          dimnames = list(colnames(lineage), colnames(lineage)))
  
  for(i in 1:ncol(lineage)) {
    for (j in i:ncol(lineage)) {
      module1 <- names(lineage)[i]
      module2 <- names(lineage)[j]
      lineage1 <- lineage[, module1]
      lineage2 <- lineage[,module2]
      
      results <- HighHighLowLow(gene_list1 = lineage1, gene_list2 = lineage2)
      
      pval <- -log10(as.numeric(results[1]))
      mean_dif <- results[2]
      
      if(mean_dif < 0) {
        pval = -pval
      }
      
      result_matrix[i,j] <- pval
      result_matrix[j,i] <- pval
    }
  }
  
  # adding NA values in the diagonal (same cell x same cell)
  diag(result_matrix) <- NA
  
  return(result_matrix)
}
```

```{r Run Two Lineage High High Low Low Matrix}
hhll <- TwoLineageMatrixHHLL(lineage = lineage_markers)
```

```{r Plot Two Lineage High/High Low/Low Heat Map}
annotated_matrix <- matrix("", nrow = nrow(hhll), ncol = ncol(hhll))
annotated_matrix[abs(hhll) > -log10(0.05)] <- "*"
annotated_matrix[abs(hhll) > -log10(0.01)] <- "**"
annotated_matrix[abs(hhll) > -log10(0.001)] <- "***"

ramp <- colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(5, "RdBu"))
mr <- ramp(1000)[1000:1]
title <- paste0(cancer, " High/High vs Low/Low")

plot <- pheatmap::pheatmap(hhll, color = mr, fontsize_col = 7, fontsize_row = 7,
                           border_color = NA, cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = FALSE,
                           main = title, display_numbers = annotated_matrix,
                           number_format = "%.5f", breaks = seq(-3, 3, length.out = 1000))

ggsave(filename = paste0(cancer, '_hihi_lowlow_heatmap.pdf'), plot = plot, dpi = 300, units = 'in',
       width = 12, height = 12)
```

# High Not High
`TwoLineageHeatMapHNH()` runs the same matrix as HHLL, but on patients that are
high in one cell type and not high in the other.
```{r Define Two Lineage High Not High Matrix}
TwoLineageMatrixHNH <- function(lineage) {
  
  # result matrix to store all the p-values 
  result_matrix <- matrix(nrow = ncol(lineage), ncol = ncol(lineage),
                          dimnames = list(colnames(lineage), colnames(lineage)))
  for(i in 1:ncol(lineage)) {
    for (j in 1:ncol(lineage)) {
      module1 <- names(lineage)[i]
      module2 <- names(lineage)[j]
      lineage1 <- lineage[, module1]
      lineage2 <- lineage[,module2]
      
      results <- HighNotHigh(gene_list1 = lineage1, gene_list2 = lineage2)
      
      pval <- -log10(as.numeric(results[1]))
      mean_dif <- results[2]
      
      # positive if mean_dif > 0, negative if mean_dif < 0
      result_matrix[i,j] <- pval * sign(mean_dif)
    }
  }
  
  # adding NA values in the diagonal (same cell x same cell)
  diag(result_matrix) <- NA
  
  return(result_matrix)
}
```

```{r Run High Not High Matrix}
hnh <- TwoLineageMatrixHNH(lineage = lineage_markers)
```

# Categorized Interactions
The purpose of `TwoLineageMatrixHHLL()` and `TwoLineageMatrixHNH()` is to
determine which cell type drives the interaction. For instance, say that
patients with high levels of two cell types have better survival. If patients
also have better survival when one of the cell types is high while the other
one is not, the high cell type is probably the one driving the positive effect
on survival.

Using this logic, we create a categorized interactions heat map which plots
which cell is responsible for driving the effect on survival.
```{r Define Categorized Interactions Function}
PlotCategorizedInteractions <- function(hhll, hnh, threshold = -log10(0.05)) {
  n <- nrow(hhll)
  
  # Initialize result_matrix with 0s
  result_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = n, ncol = n, dimnames = dimnames(hhll))
  
  # Loop over all i, j combinations
  for (i in 1:n) {
    for (j in 1:n) {
      
      # a is the combined interaction, b is high in cell 1 only, c is high in cell 2 only
      a <- hhll[i, j]
      b <- hnh[i, j]
      c <- hnh[j, i]
      
      # Skip if any required value is NA
      if (is.na(a) || is.na(b) || is.na(c)) next
      
      sig_a <- abs(a) > threshold
      sig_b <- abs(b) > threshold
      sig_c <- abs(c) > threshold
      
      
      # If only cell A is significant, cell A drives
      if (sig_a && sig_b && !sig_c) {
        result_matrix[i, j] <- 1
      }
      # If only cell B is significant, cell B drives
      else if (sig_a && !sig_b && sig_c) {
        result_matrix[i, j] <- 2
      }
      # If neither cell is significant, they work together
      else if (sig_a && !sig_b && !sig_c) {
        result_matrix[i, j] <- 3
      } 
      # If the combination takes away the significance of both cells or the 
      # one of the cells is significant in the wrong direction
      else if ((!sig_a && sig_b && sig_c) || ((a * b < 0) && sig_a && sig_b && sig_c) ||
               ((a * c < 0) && sig_a && sig_b && sig_c)) {
        result_matrix[i, j] <- 4 # mutually antagonistic
      }
    }
  }
  
  diag(result_matrix) <- NA
  
  # Define breaks for values -4 to 4
  breaks <- c(-0.5, 0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5)
  
  # Define colors for each category (-4 to 4)
  colors <- c(  
    "white",        # 0
    "navy",       # 1
    "firebrick4",        # 2
    "goldenrod1", #3
    "chartreuse3") 
  
  
  legend_breaks <- c(0,1,2,3,4)
  legend_labels <- c("", "Cell 1 Drives", "Cell 2 Drives", "Synergistic", "Antagonistic")
  
  title <- paste0(cancer, " Categorized Interactions")
  
  # Plot heatmap
  plot <- pheatmap::pheatmap(result_matrix, color = colors, breaks = breaks,
                             cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = FALSE,
                             legend_breaks = legend_breaks, legend_labels = legend_labels,
                             display_numbers = FALSE, main = title, fontsize_col = 7,
                             fontsize_row = 7, border_color = "grey")
  return(plot)
}
```

```{r Run Categorized Interactions}
p <- PlotCategorizedInteractions(hhll, hnh)

ggsave(file = paste0(cancer, '_marginal_effects.pdf'), plot = p, dpi = 300, units = 'in',
       width = 12, height = 12)
```


# Forest Plot
For the forest plot, we compare the hazard ratios of each cell type. As
explained previously, a larger hazard ratio corresponds to better survival for
the high group, while a lower hazard ratio means worse survival. The forest plot
shows the confidence intervals for the hazard ratios of each cell type, along
with listing the p value and false discovery rate (FDR).

```{r Permutation Test}
permuteSingleLineage <- function(cell) {
  baseline <- log(singleLineage(gene_list = lineage_markers[[cell]], HR = TRUE)[1])
  
  F_emp <- numeric(0)
  
  for (i in 1:1000) {
    shuffled_clinical <- clinical_data
    shuffled_clinical$cases <- sample(shuffled_clinical$cases)
    
    F_emp[i] <- log(singleLineage(gene_list = lineage_markers[[cell]], clinical = shuffled_clinical, HR = TRUE)[1])
  }
  
  return(mean(abs(F_emp) >= abs(baseline), na.rm = T))
}
```

```{r}
singleLineageForestPlot <- function(lineage) {
  
  nThreads <- detectCores() - 1
  cl <- makeCluster(nThreads)
  
  clusterSetRNGStream(cl, iseed = 777)
  
  clusterExport(cl, varlist = c("singleLineage", "permuteSingleLineage", 
                                "clinical_data", "lineage_markers", 
                                "counts", "gene_metadata"))
  
  clusterEvalQ(cl, {
    library(survival) 
    library(tidyverse)
  })
  
  cells <- colnames(lineage)
  temp <- parLapply(cl, cells, function(cell) {
    result <- singleLineage(gene_list = lineage[[cell]], HR = TRUE)
    permuted_p <- permuteSingleLineage(cell)
    return(c(cell, result[1:3], permuted_p))
  })
  
  stopCluster(cl)
  
  # --- Data Formatting ---
  result_matrix <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, temp))
  
  colnames(result_matrix) <- c("cell", "HR", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "pval")
  
  result_matrix$HR <- 1/as.numeric(result_matrix$HR)
  result_matrix$pval <- as.numeric(result_matrix$pval)
  result_matrix$ci_lower <- 1/as.numeric(result_matrix$ci_lower)
  result_matrix$ci_upper <- 1/as.numeric(result_matrix$ci_upper)
  result_matrix$padj <- p.adjust(result_matrix$pval, method = "BH")
  
  result_matrix <- result_matrix %>% 
    arrange(desc(HR)) %>% 
    filter(pval < 0.05)

  # --- Plotting Preparation ---
  estimates <- matrix(c(NA, round(result_matrix$HR, 3)), ncol = 1)
  lower <- matrix(c(NA, round(result_matrix$ci_lower,3)), ncol = 1)
  upper <- matrix(c(NA, round(result_matrix$ci_upper,3)), ncol = 1)
  
  formatted_pval <- ifelse(result_matrix$pval < 0.001, "< 0.001", round(result_matrix$pval,3))
  formatted_padj <- ifelse(result_matrix$padj < 0.001, "< 0.001", round(result_matrix$padj,3))
  
  tabletext <- cbind(
    c("Cell", result_matrix$cell),
    c("HR (95% CI)", paste0(round(as.numeric(result_matrix$HR),3), " (",
                            round(as.numeric(result_matrix$ci_upper),3), "–",
                            round(as.numeric(result_matrix$ci_lower),3), ")")),
    c("P-value", formatted_pval)
  )
  
  colnames(tabletext) <- c("Cell", "HR[95%CI]", "pval")
  tabletext <- as.matrix(tabletext)
  
  grid.newpage()
  pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(1, 1,
                                             widths = unit(1, "npc"),
                                             heights = unit(1, "npc"),
                                             respect = TRUE,
                                             just = "center"
  )))
  
  # --- Final Plot ---
  forestplot(
    labeltext = as.matrix(tabletext),
    mean  = estimates,
    lower = upper,
    upper = lower,
    zero  = 1,
    xlog  = FALSE,
    boxsize = 0.4,
    col = forestplot::fpColors(box = "black", line = "black", summary = "black"),
    lineheight = unit(0.8, "cm"),
    xticks = c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3),
    xlab = "HR",
    txt_gp = fpTxtGp(
      label = gpar(cex = 0.8),   # row labels
      xlab  = gpar(cex = 0.9),
      ticks = gpar(cex = 0.8)
    )
  )
}
```
